readings.title: The Conspiracy at Shechem
readings.subtitle: The Parable of Yotham
readings.text:
[Judges 9:1] And Aḇimeleḵ son of Yerubba‛al went to Sheḵem, to his mother’s brothers, and spoke with them and with all the clan of the house of his mother’s father, saying,
[2] “Please speak in the hearing of all the masters of Sheḵem, ‘Which is better for you, that seventy men, all the sons of Yerubba‛al rule over you, or that one man rule over you?’ And you shall remember that I am your own flesh and bone.”
[3] And his mother’s brothers spoke <dn>את</dn> all these words concerning him in the hearing of all the masters of Sheḵem. And their heart inclined toward Aḇimeleḵ, for they said, “He is our brother.”
[4] And they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Ba‛al-Berith, with which Aḇimeleḵ hired worthless and reckless men. And they followed him.
[5] And he went to his father’s house at Ophrah and killed <dn>את</dn> his brothers, the seventy sons of Yerubba‛al, on one stone. But Yotham the youngest son of Yerubba‛al was left, because he hid himself.
[6] And all the masters of Sheḵem gathered together, and all of Běyth Millo, and they went and made <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ sovereign beside the terebinth tree at the post that was in Sheḵem.
[7] And they informed Yotham, and he went and stood on top of Mount Gerizim, and lifted his voice and cried out, and said to them, “Hear me, you masters of Sheḵem, and let <dn>Elohim</dn> hear you!
[8] “The trees went forth to anoint a sovereign over them. And they said to the olive tree, ‘reign over us!’
[9] “And the olive tree said to them, ‘Shall I leave <dn>את</dn> my oil, with which they esteem mighty ones and men, and go to sway over trees?’
[10] “Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come, reign over us!’
[11] “And the fig tree said to them, ‘Shall I leave <dn>את</dn> my sweetness and <dn>את</dn> my good fruit, and go to sway over trees?’
[12] “Then the trees said to the vine, ‘Come, reign over us!’
[13] “And the vine said to them, ‘Shall I leave <dn>את</dn> my new wine, which rejoices mighty ones and men, and go to sway over trees?’
[14] “Then all the trees said to the bramble, ‘Come, reign over us!’
[15] “And the bramble said to the trees, ‘If in truth you anoint <dn>את</dn> me as sovereign over you, come, take shelter in my shade. But if not, let fire come out of the bramble and devour <dn>את</dn> the cedars of Leḇanon!’
[16] “And now, if you have acted in truth and integrity in setting up <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ to reign, and if you have acted well with Yerubba‛al and his house, and have done to him as his hands did to you –
[17] for my father fought for you and risked <dn>את</dn> his life, and delivered <dn>את</dn> you out of the hand of Miḏyan,
[18] but you have risen up against my father’s house today, and killed <dn>את</dn> his seventy sons on one stone, and set up <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ, the son of his female servant, to reign over the masters of Sheḵem, because he is your brother –
[19] if then you have acted in truth and integrity with Yerubba‛al and with his house this day, then rejoice in Aḇimeleḵ, and let him also rejoice in you.
[20] “But if not, let fire come out from Aḇimeleḵ and devour <dn>את</dn> the masters of Sheḵem and <dn>את</dn> Běyth Millo, and let fire come out from the masters of Sheḵem and from Běyth Millo and devour <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ!”
[21] Then Yotham ran away and fled, and he went to Be’ěr and dwelt there, for fear of Aḇimeleḵ his brother.

readings.title: The Treachery of Shechem
readings.subtitle: Ga'al's Rebellion and Divine Retribution
readings.text:
[Judges 9:22] And Aḇimeleḵ governed Yisra’ěl three years,
[23] and <dn>Elohim</dn> sent an evil spirit between Aḇimeleḵ and the masters of Sheḵem. And the masters of Sheḵem acted treacherously against Aḇimeleḵ,
[24] in order that the violence done to the seventy sons of Yerubba‛al might come, and their blood be laid on Aḇimeleḵ their brother, who killed <dn>את</dn> them, and on the masters of Sheḵem, who strengthened <dn>את</dn> his hands to kill <dn>את</dn> his brothers.
[25] And the masters of Sheḵem set men in ambush against him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed <dn>את</dn> all who passed over by them along that way. And it was reported to Aḇimeleḵ.
[26] And Ga‛al son of Eḇeḏ came with his brothers and passed over to Sheḵem. And the masters of Sheḵem put their trust in him,
[27] and went out into the fields, and gathered <dn>את</dn> their vineyards and trod out, and held a feast. And they went into the house of their mighty one, and ate and drank, and cursed <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ.
[28] And Ga‛al son of Eḇeḏ said, “Who is Aḇimeleḵ, and who is Sheḵem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Yerubba‛al, and is not Zeḇul his officer? Serve <dn>את</dn> the men of Ḥamor the father of Sheḵem! But why should we serve him?
[29] “If only <dn>את</dn> this people were under my hand! Then I would remove <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ.” And he said to Aḇimeleḵ, “Increase your army and come out!”
[30] And when Zeḇul, the governor of the city, heard <dn>את</dn> the words of Ga‛al son of Eḇeḏ, his displeasure burned.
[31] And he sent messengers to Aḇimeleḵ by deceit, saying, “See, Ga‛al son of Eḇeḏ and his brothers have come to Sheḵem. And see, they are besieging <dn>את</dn> the city against you.
[32] “And now, get up by night, you and the people who are with <dn>את</dn> you, and lie in wait in the field.
[33] “And it shall be, as soon as the sun is up in the morning, then rise early and rush upon the city. And see, when he and the people who are with <dn>את</dn> him come out against you, you shall do to them as your hand finds to do.”
[34] And Aḇimeleḵ and all the people who were with him rose up by night, and laid in wait against Sheḵem in four companies.
[35] Now Ga‛al son of Eḇeḏ went out and stood in the entrance to the city gate, and Aḇimeleḵ and the people who were with <dn>את</dn> him rose from lying in wait.
[36] And when Ga‛al saw <dn>את</dn> the people, he said to Zeḇul, “See, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains!” But Zeḇul said to him, “You are seeing <dn>את</dn> the shadows of the mountains like men.”
[37] And Ga‛al spoke again and said, “See, people are coming down from the high part of the land, and another company is coming from the Diviners’ Terebinth Tree.”
[38] And Zeḇul said to him, “Now where is your mouth with which you said, ‘Who is Aḇimeleḵ, that we should serve him?’ Are not these the people whom you despised? I beg you, go out and fight them now.”
[39] So Ga‛al went out, leading the masters of Sheḵem, and fought Aḇimeleḵ.
[40] And Aḇimeleḵ pursued him, and he fled from him. And many fell wounded, up to the entrance of the gate.
[41] And Aḇimeleḵ stayed at Arumah, and Zeḇul drove out <dn>את</dn> Ga‛al and <dn>את</dn> his brothers, so that they would not dwell in Sheḵem.
[42] And it came to be the next day that the people went out into the field, and they informed Aḇimeleḵ.
[43] And he took <dn>את</dn> his people, and divided them into three companies, and laid in wait in the field, and looked and saw the people coming out of the city. And he rose against them and struck them.
[44] And Aḇimeleḵ and the company that was with him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city. And the other two companies rushed upon all who were in the fields and struck them.
[45] And Aḇimeleḵ fought against the city all that day, and captured <dn>את</dn> the city and killed <dn>את</dn> the people who were in it. And he broke down <dn>את</dn> the city and sowed it with salt.
[46] And all the masters of the tower of Sheḵem had heard that, and entered the stronghold of the house of <dn>Ěl</dn> Berith.
[47] And it was reported to Aḇimeleḵ that all the masters of the tower of Sheḵem were gathered together.
[48] So Aḇimeleḵ went up to Mount Tsalmon, he and all the people who were with <dn>את</dn> him. And Aḇimeleḵ took <dn>את</dn> an axe in his hand and cut down a branch from the trees, and took it and laid it on his shoulder. Then he said to the people who were with him, “What you have seen me do, hurry, do as I have done.”
[49] And all the people likewise cut down each one his own branch and followed Aḇimeleḵ, and put them against the stronghold, and set <dn>את</dn> the stronghold on fire above them, so that all the men of the tower of Sheḵem died, about a thousand men and women.
[50] Aḇimeleḵ then went to Thěḇěts, and he encamped against Thěḇěts and captured it.
[51] However, there was a strong tower in the city, and all the men and women and all the masters of the city fled there and shut themselves in, and went up to the top of the tower.
[52] And Aḇimeleḵ came to the tower and fought against it, and approached the door of the tower to burn it with fire.
[53] But a certain woman dropped an upper millstone on the head of Aḇimeleḵ, and crushed <dn>את</dn> his skull.
[54] He then immediately called the young man, his armour-bearer, and said to him, “Draw your sword and kill me, lest men say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’ ” And his young man thrust him through, and he died.
[55] And when the men of Yisra’ěl saw that Aḇimeleḵ was dead, each one went to his own place.
[56] Thus did <dn>Elohim</dn> repay <dn>את</dn> the evil of Aḇimeleḵ, which he had done to his father to kill <dn>את</dn> his seventy brothers.
[57] And <dn>את</dn> all the evil of the men of Sheḵem <dn>Elohim</dn> turned back on their own heads, and the curse of Yotham son of Yerubba‛al came on them.

readings.title: Tola and Yair
readings.subtitle: Periods of Rest in Israel
readings.text:
[Judges 10:1] And after Aḇimeleḵ there arose Tola son of Pu’ah, son of Doḏo, a man of Yissasḵar, to save <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl. And he dwelt in Shamur in the mountains of Ephrayim.
[2] And he ruled <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried in Shamur.
[3] And after him arose Ya’ir, a Gil‛aḏite, and he ruled <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl twenty-two years.
[4] And he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys. And they had thirty towns, which are called Havoth Yair to this day, which are in the land of Gil‛aḏ.
[5] And Ya’ir died, and was buried in Qamon.

readings.title: Israel's Apostasy and Distress
readings.subtitle: The Cry for Deliverance
readings.text:
[Judges 10:6] And the children of Yisra’ěl again did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and served <dn>את</dn> the Ba‛als and <dn>את</dn> the Ashtoreths, and <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of Aram, and <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of Tsiḏon, and <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of Mo’aḇ, and <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of the children of Ammon, and <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of the Philistines – and forsook <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and did not serve <dn>Him</dn>.
[7] Therefore the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Yisra’ěl. And <dn>He</dn> sold them into the hands of the Philistines and into the hands of the children of Ammon.
[8] And they crushed and oppressed <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl that year – for eighteen years – all <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl who were beyond the Yarděn in the land of the Amorites, in Gil‛aḏ.
[9] And the children of Ammon passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn to fight against Yehuḏah, and against Binyamin, and against the house of Ephrayim, so that Yisra’ěl had great distress.
[10] And the children of Yisra’ěl cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “We have sinned against <dn>You</dn>, because we have both forsaken <dn>את</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> and served <dn>את</dn> the Ba‛als!”
[11] So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to the children of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“Was it not from the Mitsrites and from the Amorites and from the children of Ammon and from the Philistines that <dn>I</dn> saved you?</dq>
[12] <dq>“And the Tsiḏonians and Amalěq and Ma‛on oppressed <dn>את</dn> you. And you cried out to <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> you from their hand.</dq>
[13] <dq>“But you, you have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn> and served other mighty ones. Therefore <dn>I</dn> do not save <dn>את</dn> you again.</dq>
[14] <dq>“Go and cry out to the mighty ones which you have chosen, let them save you in your time of distress.”</dq>
[15] And the children of Yisra’ěl said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “We have sinned! Do to us whatever is good in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, only deliver us today, please.”
[16] So they put away <dn>את</dn> the foreign mighty ones from their midst and served <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>His</dn> being was grieved with the trouble of Yisra’ěl.
[17] Then the children of Ammon were called together and encamped in Gil‛aḏ. And the children of Yisra’ěl gathered together and encamped in Mitspah.
[18] And the people, the heads of Gil‛aḏ, said to each other, “Let the man who is the first to fight against the children of Ammon be head over all the inhabitants of Gil‛aḏ.”

readings.title: The Outcast Commander
readings.subtitle: Negotiations with Ammon
readings.text:
[Judges 11:1] And Yiphtaḥ the Gil‛aḏite was a mighty brave one, but he was the son of a whore. And Gil‛aḏ brought forth <dn>את</dn> Yiphtaḥ.
[2] And the wife of Gil‛aḏ bore sons. And when his wife’s sons grew up, they drove <dn>את</dn> Yiphtaḥ out, and said to him, “You shall not have an inheritance in the house of our father, for you are the son of another woman.”
[3] And Yiphtaḥ fled from his brothers and dwelt in the land of Toḇ. And worthless men banded together with Yiphtaḥ and went out with him.
[4] And it came to be, some time later, that the children of Ammon fought against Yisra’ěl.
[5] And it came to be, when the children of Ammon fought against Yisra’ěl, that the elders of Gil‛aḏ went to bring <dn>את</dn> Yiphtaḥ out of the land of Toḇ.
[6] And they said to Yiphtaḥ, “Come, and you shall be our commander, and let us fight against the children of Ammon.”
[7] But Yiphtaḥ said to the elders of Gil‛aḏ, “Did you not hate <dn>את</dn> me, and drive me from my father’s house? Why have you come to me now when you are in trouble?”
[8] And the elders of Gil‛aḏ said to Yiphtaḥ, “That is the reason we have turned to you, that you shall go with us and fight against the children of Ammon, and be our head over all the inhabitants of Gil‛aḏ.”
[9] And Yiphtaḥ said to the elders of Gil‛aḏ, “If you take <dn>את</dn> me back home to fight against the children of Ammon, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gives <dn>את</dn> them to me, am I to be your head?”
[10] And the elders of Gil‛aḏ said to Yiphtaḥ, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is witness between us, if we do not do according to your words.”
[11] Then Yiphtaḥ went with the elders of Gil‛aḏ, and the people set <dn>את</dn> him over them, as head and commander. And Yiphtaḥ spoke <dn>את</dn> all his words before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Mitspah.
[12] And Yiphtaḥ sent messengers to the sovereign of the children of Ammon, saying, “What is between you and me, that you have come to fight against me in my land?”
[13] And the sovereign of the children of Ammon said to the messengers of Yiphtaḥ, “Because Yisra’ěl took <dn>את</dn> my land when they came up out of Mitsrayim, from the Arnon as far as the Yabboq, and to the Yarděn. And now, give back <dn>את</dn> those lands in peace.”
[14] But Yiphtaḥ again sent messengers to the sovereign of the children of Ammon,
[15] and said to him, “This is what Yiphtaḥ said, ‘Yisra’ěl did not take <dn>את</dn> the land of Mo’aḇ, nor <dn>את</dn> the land of the children of Ammon.
[16] For when they came up from Mitsrayim, and Yisra’ěl walked through the wilderness as far as the Sea of Reeds and came to Qaḏěsh,
[17] then Yisra’ěl sent messengers to the sovereign of Eḏom, saying, “Please let me pass over, through your land.” But the sovereign of Eḏom would not listen. And they also sent to the sovereign of Mo’aḇ, but he refused, so Yisra’ěl stayed at Qaḏěsh.
[18] Then they went through the wilderness and around <dn>את</dn> the land of Eḏom and <dn>את</dn> the land of Mo’aḇ, and came to the east side of the land of Mo’aḇ, and encamped beyond Arnon. But they did not enter the border of Mo’aḇ, for Arnon was the border of Mo’aḇ.
[19] And Yisra’ěl sent messengers to Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, sovereign of Ḥeshbon, and Yisra’ěl said to him, “Please let us pass over, through your land into our place.”
[20] But Siḥon did not trust <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl to pass over through his border, and Siḥon gathered <dn>את</dn> all his people together, and they encamped in Yahats, and fought against Yisra’ěl.
[21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl gave <dn>את</dn> Siḥon and <dn>את</dn> all his people into the hand of Yisra’ěl, and they struck them. So Yisra’ěl took possession of <dn>את</dn> all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that land.
[22] Thus they took possession of <dn>את</dn> all the border of the Amorites, from Arnon to the Yabboq and from the wilderness to the Yarděn.
[23] And now, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl has driven out <dn>את</dn> the Amorites from before <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ěl, should you then possess it?
[24] <dn>את</dn> Whatever Kemosh your mighty one gives you to possess, do you not possess it? And <dn>את</dn> all that which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> takes possession of before us, we possess.
[25] And now are you any better than Balaq son of Tsippor, sovereign of Mo’aḇ? Did he ever strive against Yisra’ěl? Did he ever fight against them?
[26] While Yisra’ěl dwelt in Ḥeshbon and its villages, and in Aro‛ěr and its villages, and in all the cities along the banks of Arnon, for three hundred years, why did you not recover them within that time?
[27] So I have not sinned against you, but you are doing me evil by fighting against me. Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the Judge, judge today between the children of Yisra’ěl and the children of Ammon.’ ”
[28] But the sovereign of the children of Ammon did not listen to the words which Yiphtaḥ sent him.

readings.title: Victory over Ammon
readings.subtitle: The Tragic Fulfillment
readings.text:
[Judges 11:29] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon Yiphtaḥ, and he passed through <dn>את</dn> Gil‛aḏ and <dn>את</dn> Menashsheh, and passed through <dn>את</dn> Mitspeh of Gil‛aḏ. And from Mitspeh of Gil‛aḏ he passed on toward the children of Ammon.
[30] And Yiphtaḥ made a vow to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “If <dn>You</dn> give <dn>את</dn> the children of Ammon into my hands,
[31] then it shall be that whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, shall belong to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and I shall offer it up as an ascending offering.”
[32] Yiphtaḥ then passed on toward the children of Ammon to fight against them, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave them into his hands.
[33] And he struck them from Aro‛ěr as far as Minnith, twenty cities, and to Aḇěl Keramim, with a very great slaughter. Thus the children of Ammon were humbled before the children of Yisra’ěl.
[34] And Yiphtaḥ came to his house at Mitspah, and saw his daughter coming out to meet him with timbrels and dancing. Now except for her he had neither son nor daughter.
[35] And it came to be, when he saw <dn>את</dn> her, that he tore <dn>את</dn> his garments, and said, “Oh my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you are among those who trouble me! And I, I have given my word to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and I am unable to turn back.”
[36] And she said to him, “My father, if you have given <dn>את</dn> your word to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do to me according to what has gone out of your mouth, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has taken vengeance for you upon your enemies, the children of Ammon.”
[37] And she said to her father, “Let this be done for me: let me alone for two new moons, and let me go and wander on the mountains and bewail my maidenhood, my friends and I.”
[38] Then he said, “Go.” And he sent <dn>את</dn> her away for two new moons. And she went with her friends, and bewailed her maidenhood on the mountains.
[39] And it came to be at the end of two new moons that she returned to her father, and he did to her <dn>את</dn> as he had vowed, and she knew no man. And it became a statute in Yisra’ěl
[40] that the daughters of Yisra’ěl went every year for four days to lament the daughter of Yiphtaḥ the Gil‛aḏite.
